references.text: The law was given through Moses at Sinai. [ref:2 Mos 20:1-17|Exodus 20:1-17] describes the Ten Commandments given to the people through Moses, which John refers to with the words "the law was given by Moses".

In [ref:2 Mos 34:6|Exodus 34:6], the Lord reveals Himself to Moses as "merciful and gracious ... abundant in lovingkindness and truth (חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת)". The expression "grace and truth" (χάρις καὶ ἀλήθεια) in John 1:17 reflects precisely this Old Testament pair of concepts.
In [ref:2 Mos 34:28|Exodus 34:28], it is confirmed that the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments, were written on stone tablets. This emphasizes that the law was delivered through Moses.
[ref:5 Mos 4:44|Deuteronomy 4:44] states that "this is the law which Moses set before the children of Israel", confirming that the law was given by Moses.
[ref:5 Mos 33:4|Deuteronomy 33:4] says, "Moses commanded us a law, an inheritance for the congregation of Jacob", a direct parallel to the fact that the law was given through Moses.

[ref:Joh 1:14|John 1:14] states that the Word became flesh and was "full of grace and truth". Verse 17 elaborates on this by contrasting the giving of the law through Moses with the coming of grace and truth through Jesus Christ.

[ref:Joh 1:16|John 1:16] speaks of how "from his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace". Verse 17 explains this further: the law came through Moses, but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
In [ref:Joh 5:46|John 5:46], Jesus says: "If you believed Moses, you would believe me; for he wrote of me." Moses and the law point forward to Jesus Christ, who brought grace and truth.
In [ref:Joh 8:32|John 8:32], Jesus says: "You will know the truth, and the truth will set you free." The truth that came through Jesus Christ (John 1:17) is liberating truth.
Jesus says in [ref:Joh 14:6|John 14:6]: "I am the way, the truth, and the life." The truth that came through Jesus Christ (John 1:17) shows that He Himself is the truth in person.

[ref:Rom 3:24|Romans 3:24] teaches that we "are justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus". The unmerited grace that came through Jesus Christ is the core of John 1:17.

[ref:Rom 5:21|Romans 5:21] speaks of how "grace might reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord". Paul emphasizes, just as John does, that grace comes through Jesus Christ.
[ref:Rom 6:14|Romans 6:14] says, "you are not under law but under grace." This reflects the same contrast between law and grace that John draws in 1:17.

[ref:Rom 10:4|Romans 10:4] states that "Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes". This elaborates on the contrast in John 1:17: the law came through Moses, but Christ is the fulfillment of the law.
[ref:Gal 3:19|Galatians 3:19] explains that the law "was put in place through angels by an intermediary", namely Moses. Paul confirms what John says about the delivery of the law through Moses.
[ref:Tit 2:11|Titus 2:11] states that "the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people". The grace made real through Jesus Christ in John 1:17 is the same saving grace Paul speaks of.
